generations.name: Fifth generation
generations.note: The 'fluidic sculpture' car that made the segment look twice. Sharp styling, strong value, and the generation where Elantra stopped being the default rental and started being a choice.

generations.name: Sixth generation
generations.note: Calmer styling, better refinement, and a Sport model with a 1.6L turbo and independent rear suspension — a quiet preview of what the N division would do properly later.

generations.name: Seventh generation
generations.note: Origami styling and, at the top, the Elantra N: 276 hp, a limited-slip differential, and a dual-clutch or manual. It embarrasses hot hatches costing far more, on track days especially.

models.intro: Hyundai's compact started as transport for people who couldn't afford a Civic and ended up producing the Elantra N, one of the best performance bargains on sale. That arc is Hyundai's last 30 years in miniature.
models.name: Elantra

generations.name: Sixth generation
generations.note: The styling shock of 2011 — a midsize sedan that looked like a concept car — paired with a 2.0L turbo making 274 hp, more than the V6 rivals it replaced.

generations.name: Seventh generation
generations.note: Hyundai turned the drama down and the quality up: better ride, better materials, a 245 hp turbo flagship. Less memorable to look at, more car to own.

generations.name: Eighth generation
generations.note: The drama came back: a full-width light treatment and an N Line with a 290 hp 2.5L turbo. Hybrids now do most of the sales, which suits the car fine.

models.intro: The car that announced Hyundai could design. The 2011 Sonata's swooping styling forced every midsize rival to follow, and the current car splits its personality between efficient hybrids and a properly quick N Line.
models.name: Sonata

generations.name: First generation
generations.note: Built on Hyundai's dedicated E-GMP electric platform with 800-volt charging — 10 to 80 percent in under 20 minutes in ideal conditions. The dual-motor car makes 320 hp; the Ioniq 5 N turns it into a 641 hp track-capable machine with fake gearshifts that somehow work.

models.intro: A retro-futuristic hatchback the size of a crossover, and the car that made Hyundai a design leader in the EV era. Pixel lights, a flat floor, and charging speeds that embarrassed cars costing twice as much at launch.
models.name: Ioniq 5

generations.name: First generation
generations.note: Hyundai's first compact SUV for the global push: unibody, car-like manners, and an optional 2.7L V6. Anonymous to look at, significant in hindsight.

generations.name: Third generation
generations.note: Sharper styling, a turbocharged option, and the polish that made Tucson a default shortlist car rather than a budget alternative. The segment's centre of gravity had moved, and Hyundai moved with it.

generations.name: Fourth generation
generations.note: Concept-car styling, a hybrid and plug-in hybrid in the range from launch, and an interior that went fully digital. The hybrid is the sweet spot of the lineup.

models.intro: Hyundai's RAV4 and CR-V rival, and the model that shows how far the mainstream range has come: the current hybrid is efficient, quick enough, and styled like it escaped from a motor show stand.
models.name: Tucson
